patient._comment: 'patient' contains the three sections that may be exposed in the detailed patient display: presentation, answer, and clinical.

presentation._comment: The immutable patient evidence package available for triage. Panel context controls whether other sections are locked or available.
presentation.quote: (Bystander) She dropped and started convulsing — full-body shaking for a couple of minutes, bit her tongue. It stopped on its own. She's coming around now but she's groggy and confused.
presentation.triageNote: 35-year-old female who suddenly collapsed and had about two minutes of whole-body stiffening and shaking witnessed by a bystander. She bit her tongue; the movements stopped spontaneously and she is now groggy but rousable.

answer._comment: The authoritative game answer. Explicit ESI, destination, and destination rationale are answer-bearing content; the player's assignment remains session state.
answer.destinationReason: ESI 2 is appropriate because the patient remains postictal and groggy after a generalized seizure, making altered responsiveness a high-risk neurologic presentation.

clinical._comment: Display-ready clinical interpretation derived from patient.presentation. It preserves clinical meaning but must not explicitly name or identify the correct ESI level or destination; it does not participate in scoring.
clinical.summary: This patient had a witnessed two-minute generalized convulsion with tongue injury and remains groggy but rousable.
clinical.acuityReason: The seizure has stopped and breathing is maintained, but she has not returned to neurologic baseline and needs prompt reassessment for recurrence and cause.
expectedResources: Brain imaging or toxicologic testing when indicated
keyFindings: Two minutes of generalized stiffening and shaking
teachingPoints: Glucose should be checked promptly in every seizure presentation.
Ongoing seizure activity or failure to recover may require immediate anticonvulsant and airway treatment.

possibleClinicalOutcome.disposition: Prompt assessment and observation would determine whether recovery permits discharge or whether imaging, treatment, and admission are required.

aiImageGeneration._comment: 'aiImageGeneration' is info for AI to generate the image of the patient. Most images were done with openAI gpt-image-1 using an API, not the app, in July 2026. Look for some python scripts that are used to create these images. Be sure that the anchor-image is available and is provided to the AI - otherwise the images will not be consistent.
aiImageGeneration.pose: slumped and dazed, being supported in the chair
signs: a little blood at the lip
aiImageGeneration.prompt: Softly-shaded painterly cartoon illustration in a semi-realistic Pixar/Disney style: smooth gradient shading, soft natural lighting, gentle rounded volumes, fine delicate outlines (NOT thick flat cartoon outlines), warm detailed rendering, natural realistic proportions, single character, 3/4 front view, centered, square 1:1. Match the exact painterly style, brushwork, shading, line weight, lighting, and palette of the attached reference image. Subject: a black 35-year-old woman, groggy and dazed, slumped on a blue padded clinic chair. Pose: slumped and supported, head heavy. Expression: dazed and confused, a postictal look. Clearly visible: an unfocused dazed gaze and a small bit of blood at the lip. No text, no logos.
